html:
The Sauk-Suiattle are a Coast Salish people of the Sauk, Suiattle and upper Skagit rivers in the Cascade foothills of western Washington, near Darrington. They speak Lushootseed.

They fished for salmon, hunted in the mountains and traded across the Cascades. They were named under the Treaty of Point Elliott of 1855 but got no reservation of their own, and many were pushed out as settlers took the valleys. Their neighbours include the Skagit, the Stillaguamish and the Snohomish. See also Coast Salish.
